incidentDetails.incidentTitle: ATM robbery via bombing — Ink/dye system not installed (Mankayane Branch)
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: The Mankayane Branch ATM was subjected to a bombing attack resulting in forceful removal of the machine. The ATM was not fitted with an ink/dye staining system, increasing exposure to unrecoverable cash loss. The matter has been reported to law enforcement and a review of ink/dye deployment across the ATM network is underway.

correctiveActions: Install ink/dye staining systems on all ATMs across the branch network, prioritising high-risk and remote locations.
Conduct a physical security assessment of all ATM sites to identify and address vulnerabilities including reinforcement of ATM housing and installation of anti-blast anchoring mechanisms.
Engage law enforcement and the security service provider to review ATM surveillance and rapid response protocols to deter and detect future incidents.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: MPOS transactions not settled — Unreconciled Mastercard Acquiring transactions since Apr 2025
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: Mastercard Acquiring transactions processed via MPOS have remained unreconciled and unsettled since April 2025, resulting in a backlog of outstanding entries. This represents a financial and operational risk to the bank and requires urgent remediation to prevent further revenue leakage and regulatory exposure.

correctiveActions: Conduct an immediate reconciliation of all unreconciled Mastercard Acquiring MPOS transactions from April 2025 to date, identify the root cause of the settlement failure and process all outstanding entries.
Implement a daily MPOS reconciliation monitoring control with assigned ownership to ensure timely detection and escalation of any future settlement breaks before they accumulate.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: Branch robbery — E1.6 million stolen, alarm system not activated
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: The Mankayane Branch was subjected to an armed robbery resulting in a cash loss of E1.6 million. The alarm system was not activated during the incident, delaying security response and contributing to the extent of the loss. The matter has been reported to law enforcement and is under investigation.

correctiveActions: Conduct an immediate investigation to determine why the alarm system was not activated during the incident and hold responsible parties accountable.
Implement a mandatory daily alarm system test at branch opening and closing, with sign-off by the branch manager as evidence of functionality.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: ATM robbery via bombing — Ink/dye system not installed (Mankayane Branch)
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: ATM robbery via explosive attack at Mankayane Branch due to absence of an ink/dye cash protection system, resulting in increased vulnerability to cash theft.

correctiveActions: Install ATM ink/dye cash protection systems at the Mankayane Branch and all high-risk ATMs to render stolen cash unusable in the event of forced access or bombing.
Enhance ATM physical security measures, including blast-resistant ATM enclosures, reinforced safes, CCTV coverage, alarm systems, and intrusion/vibration sensors linked to rapid response teams.

Conduct a branch-wide ATM security risk assessment and implement a preventive maintenance and compliance program to ensure all ATMs meet minimum security standards and critical protection systems are operational.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: MPOS transactions not settled — Unreconciled Mastercard Acquiring transactions since Apr 2025
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: MPOS transactions remain unsettled due to unreconciled Mastercard Acquiring transactions dating back to April 2025, resulting in outstanding balances and delays in financial reconciliation.

correctiveActions: Conduct a comprehensive reconciliation exercise to identify, investigate, and clear all outstanding Mastercard Acquiring MPOS transactions pending since April 2025, with documented resolution timelines.
Engage Mastercard and the acquiring/processor support team to resolve settlement failures, system integration issues, or transaction mismatches causing the unreconciled items.
Implement a daily transaction monitoring and reconciliation process with automated exception reporting and escalation protocols to ensure timely settlement and prevent future backlogs.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: Branch robbery — E1.6 million stolen, alarm system not activated
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: Branch robbery resulting in the theft of E1.6 million, exacerbated by failure to activate the alarm system, leading to delayed response and increased financial loss.

correctiveActions: Ensure mandatory alarm system activation through staff training and accountability measures.
Conduct regular testing and maintenance of alarm systems to confirm functionality at all times.
Strengthen branch security controls, including emergency response drills and enhanced surveillance monitoring.
nstall panic buttons and automated alarm triggers to ensure immediate activation during robbery incidents, reducing reliance on manual intervention.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: Transactions processed without sufficient funds or approved overdraft — Inyatsi Construction
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: Transactions processed on the Inyatsi Construction account despite insufficient funds and absence of an approved overdraft facility, resulting in unauthorized account exposure and control failure.

correctiveActions: Enforce system controls to block transactions where insufficient funds exist and no approved overdraft facility is in place.
Review and strengthen approval processes for overdrafts to ensure proper authorization and documentation before transaction processing.
Implement daily exception monitoring for unauthorized overdrafts and insufficient fund transactions with prompt escalation procedures.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: Duplicate outward clearing transactions sent to correspondent banks — manual re-execution error
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: Duplicate outward clearing transactions were sent to correspondent banks due to a manual re-execution error, resulting in duplicate processing risk and reconciliation discrepancies.

correctiveActions: Implement maker-checker controls for outward clearing transactions to prevent unauthorized or duplicate re-execution.
Enhance system validation checks to automatically detect and block duplicate transaction submissions before transmission to correspondent banks.
Provide staff training and procedural guidance on clearing processes to minimize manual processing errors and ensure adherence to approved workflows.

incidentDetails.incidentTitle: ADT deposits unsuccessful — funds returned to customer but T24 credits remain
incidentDetails.incidentDescription: ADT deposit transactions were unsuccessful, with funds returned to customers while corresponding credits remained posted in T24, resulting in duplicate credit risk and reconciliation discrepancies.

correctiveActions: Perform immediate reconciliation and reversal of outstanding T24 credits linked to unsuccessful ADT deposits to correct customer account balances.
Enhance system integration controls between ADT and T24 to ensure automatic reversal of credits when deposits fail or funds are returned.
Implement daily exception monitoring and reporting for failed ADT transactions to enable timely identification, investigation, and resolution of discrepancies.

findings.title: Review of policies and procedures
Outdated document control procedure not aligned with current process
findings.description: uring review of the Document Control Procedure (DOC-001, Rev 3), it was found that the procedure references an approval workflow that was discontinued in Q1 2026. Three policy documents (HR-Policy-04, IT-Policy-02, QA-Policy-07) were approved using the outdated workflow, bypassing the current two-stage sign-off requirement.
findings.rootCauseDetail: The procedure update following the Q1 2026 workflow change was not communicated to document owners, and the master procedure document was not revised accordingly
findings.recommendation: Revise DOC-001 to reflect the current two-stage approval workflow; re-issue for approval; retrain document owners on the updated process; re-approve the three affected policies under the correct workflow.
findings.managementResponse: Agreed. QA team will revise and re-issue DOC-001 by 15 Sep 2026, followed by a mandatory refresher training session for all document owners. The three affected policies will be re-routed for approval under the correct workflow by the target resolution date.

issues.title: No formal policy governing third-party data sharing
issues.description: The current policy library does not include a dedicated Third-Party Data Sharing Policy. Several departments (HR, Sales, IT) share data with external vendors based on informal, undocumented practices, creating inconsistency in data handling standards and potential regulatory exposure.
issues.recommendation: Draft and implement a formal Third-Party Data Sharing Policy covering vendor risk assessment, data classification, and contractual data protection clauses. Conduct a review of all existing third-party data flows against the new policy.
issues.managementResponse: Agreed. Legal and IT Security will co-draft the policy by 30 Sep 2026, with rollout and department briefings completed by the target resolution date. An interim data-sharing checklist will be issued in the meantime to reduce immediate risk.

findings.title: Missing signatures on Medication Administration Records (MAR)
findings.description: Review of 15 resident medication folders identified 4 instances where MAR charts had missing staff signatures following medication administration, with no documented reason (e.g., refusal, withheld) recorded. Gaps were found across morning and evening shifts over the past two weeks.
findings.rootCauseDetail: Staff are not consistently completing MAR sign-off immediately after administration, particularly during high-workload shift changes. No secondary check is in place to catch missed entries in real time.
findings.recommendation: Reinforce medication administration protocol requiring immediate MAR sign-off; introduce end-of-shift double-check by senior staff; retrain all care staff on MAR documentation requirements; conduct spot-checks weekly for the next month.
findings.managementResponse: Agreed. Refresher training on MAR documentation will be delivered to all care staff by 10 Aug 2026. A shift-handover checklist including MAR verification will be introduced immediately, and weekly spot-audits will be conducted by the Care Home Manager for one month to confirm compliance.

findings.title: Review of Organisational Manual
Organisational chart in manual does not reflect current reporting structure
findings.description: The organisational chart included in the Organisational Manual (Section 2, Page 8) shows an outdated reporting structure. Two department head roles created during the 2026 restructuring are not reflected, and one listed role (Regional Coordinator) was discontinued in January 2026 but still appears as active.
findings.rootCauseDetail: The Organisational Manual was not updated following the internal restructuring; there is no defined trigger or ownership for updating the manual when organisational changes occur.
findings.recommendation: Update the organisational chart and related role descriptions to reflect the current structure; establish a formal trigger requiring HR to notify the Document Controller of any structural change within 5 working days, with the manual updated accordingly.
findings.managementResponse: Agreed. HR will provide the current organisational structure to the Document Controller by 20 Aug 2026 for immediate update. A standing procedure will be added to the change management process to ensure the manual is updated within 5 working days of any future restructuring.
